about: AU Small Finance Bank Limited is engaged in providing a range of banking and financial services including retail banking, wholesale banking, treasury operations and other services. [1]

cash.note: For lenders, operating cash flow mostly reflects loan-book growth, so conversion ratios are not meaningful.

business.what: AU Small Finance Bank is an Indian bank that makes money from interest on loans across secured retail, commercial and unsecured segments, funded by deposits, with fee income and treasury gains.

segments.name: Retail secured assets (Wheels, Mortgages, Gold Loan) - loan book
segments.comment: Grew 22% YoY and 5% QoQ; Wheels crossed ₹50,000 crore, gold loans up 102% YoY.

segments.name: Commercial Banking - loan book (~₹35,300 crore)
segments.comment: Grew 39% YoY and 8% QoQ, with transaction banking and forex income up 51%.

segments.name: Unsecured businesses (Inclusive Banking/MFI, digital unsecured, personal loans, cards)
segments.comment: Grew 23% YoY and 8% QoQ; personal loans up 81% YoY off a low base.

segments.name: Branch Banking - deposits
segments.comment: Deposits grew 29% YoY; CA balances up 55%, supporting a stronger CASA mix.

ledger.promise: Loan growth of about 20-22% (2.25-2.5x nominal GDP) in FY26 and again in FY27
ledger.quote: I think anything around 20%, 22% growth overall, we are targeting, right? And that should continue for next year too
ledger.actual: No loan-book figures here. Q4 FY26 call says growth target 'we really delivered'. Revenue: FY26 +16.0%, H1 FY27 +22.8% YoY (10,915 vs 8,889).

ledger.promise: ROA of about 1.8% for full-year FY27
ledger.quote: for FY'27, we had earlier guided that our endeavor will be to try and reach 1.8. We continue to maintain that.
ledger.actual: Q4 FY26 ROA was 1.8% (called seasonal). 1.8% repeated in Q1 and Q2 FY27 calls. H1 FY27 PAT 1,654, up 44.8% YoY. No asset data to compute ROA.

ledger.quote: So, in a normalized scenario, I think NIM should settle at 6%.
ledger.actual: Q1 FY27 call dropped directional NIM guidance and said cost of funds would be 'stable to maybe increasing a little'. No NIM figure in materials.

ledger.quote: ideally, we should be in the range of 56%-57%, next year too.
ledger.actual: No cost-to-income figure in materials. Later calls stopped using this metric and gave cost-to-assets guidance instead.

ledger.promise: FY26 opex to average assets below FY25's 4.3%
ledger.quote: we will be lower than 4.3% cost to OPEX, which we were last year, right? So, this year, we expect to do better.
ledger.actual: No full-year FY26 ratio given. Q1 FY27 call cites 3.9% for the prior quarter (excl. CGFMU) and 4.0% for Q1 FY27.

ledger.promise: Cost to assets below 4% in FY27
ledger.quote: I believe next year, this current financial year, we should be lower than 4%.
ledger.actual: Q1 FY27 was 4.0%, up from 3.9%. The Q1 and Q2 FY27 calls only promise 'improve YoY' and do not repeat the below-4% figure.

ledger.promise: FY26 credit cost about 1% of average assets
ledger.quote: For FY'26, our credit cost should be in the range of 1%
ledger.actual: No FY26 credit-cost figure in materials. Q4 FY26 call says only that FY27 credit cost should be lower than FY26.

ledger.promise: FY27 credit cost lower than FY26, planned at about 90 bps
ledger.quote: if you ask me, we should build it around 90 bps or maybe in that range
ledger.actual: Q2 FY27 call: 'till September, everything has been in line', expects to stay within the guided range. Management did not disclose a figure.

ledger.promise: 80 new branches in FY26; 100+ more in FY27
ledger.quote: on track to take new branch addition tally to 80 branches for the year, mostly in urban areas.
ledger.actual: FY26 final count not stated (66 opened by Q3). Q1 FY27: 16 opened, 'on track' for 100+. Capital WIP rose from 87 (FY25) to 555 (FY26).

ledger.promise: Credit card book: stabilise over about one year, no aggressive growth
ledger.quote: Credit card, I think we want to take one more year to really stabilize it to the core
ledger.actual: Q4 FY26 call: card business 'broadly stabilized this quarter after nearly five quarters of de-growth', with gradual growth expected.

ledger.promise: Mortgage growth up from 13-15% to at least 17-18% over 2-3 years
ledger.quote: the current growth rate of 13 %-15%, we can scale it up to at least 17 %- 18% over the next 2-3 years.
ledger.actual: No segment data. Q2 FY27 call brought the target forward to 'in the range of 20% by next year'.

ledger.promise: Commercial banking book to return to growth in FY27
ledger.quote: we expect the book to return to growth in the next financial year.
ledger.actual: FY27 not yet over, and no later call or segment data reports this book's growth.

credibility.label: mixed
credibility.summary: Few promises can be checked against these materials. Of those that can, the credit card book stabilised as promised, Q4 FY26 ROA reached 1.8%, and PAT has kept rising (H1 FY27 up 44.8%). But the 6% NIM guidance was dropped, cost to assets rose to 4.0% in Q1 FY27 against a below-4% goal, and the cost-to-income and FY26 credit-cost targets were never reported back.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Q4 FY26's 1.8% ROA was seasonal and should not be seen as permanent.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: PAT did not fall back after Q4 FY26 (832): Q1 FY27 was 796 and Q2 FY27 was 858. H1 FY27 PAT of 1,654 is up 44.8% on H1 FY26 (1,142).

narrative_vs_numbers.story: The bank grows at 2-2.5x nominal GDP, about 20-22% a year, and says it 'really delivered' this.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Loan data is not available. Revenue grew 16.0% in FY26 (18,636 vs 16,064) and 17.5% YoY in Q4 FY26, then sped up to 21.1% in Q1 FY27 and 24.4% in Q2 FY27.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Cost to assets would fall below 4% in FY27, with steady improvement year on year.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: The Q1 FY27 call reported cost to assets of 4.0%, up from 3.9%. Later calls guided only to 'improve YoY'. Q3 FY26 opex excluding the labour code was already up 14% QoQ.

narrative_vs_numbers.story: Spending on headcount and branches is a 'down payment on future growth'.
narrative_vs_numbers.numbers: Capital WIP rose from 87 (FY25) to 555 (FY26), and operating cash flow fell from 5,462 to 1,829. This fits heavier investment, though bank cash flows are noisy.

bull.point: Profit growth has held up and sped up after the guidance was given.
bull.evidence: Q2 FY27 PAT was 858 vs 561 a year earlier. TTM PAT is 3,153 against FY26's 2,641.

bull.point: Management says credit cost is within the guided range, with room to spare.
bull.evidence: 'till September, everything has been in line'. Guidance of close to 90 bps leaves 'enough room for any kind of vulnerabilities or one-off'.

bull.point: Problem segments are recovering and growth targets have been raised.
bull.evidence: The card book stabilised after five quarters of shrinking (Q4 FY26 call p9). The mortgage target was brought forward from 17-18% over 2-3 years to about 20% next year (Q2 FY27 call p26).

bear.evidence: After the 6% normalised NIM talk in Q3 FY26, management said 'I don't want to give you any sort of directional guidance', and expects cost of funds to stay flat or rise a little.

bear.point: Cost targets are slipping and being softened.
bear.evidence: The Q4 FY26 call set cost to assets below 4%. Q1 FY27 came in at 4.0%, up from 3.9%, and later calls only promise a YoY improvement.

bear.point: There are unquantified risks to ROA and asset quality.
bear.evidence: The insurance fee consultation paper is a 'headwind' (Q2 FY27 p14). Coverage fell because of write-offs (Q2 FY27 p27). The ECL impact cannot be quantified until about end-Q3 (Q1 FY27 p14).
